assumptions: Laterality is unilateral with the right side working, since the instructions do not name a side.
The movement is a hang clean: powerful hip extension from a hinged start, assisted by knee extension and ankle plantarflexion, then elbow flexion to reach the rack.
The bell is held bottoms-up (inverted), so grip and wrist stability are key demands.
The shoulder raise and shrug that accompany the pull are assist actions only.
Both legs drive the hip extension, so the leg actions use sides both, while the load is held in one arm.
classification_reasons: The exercise is a standing one-arm kettlebell hang clean held bottoms-up, which the vocabulary can represent faithfully.
The contact sheet shows a hang start with the kettlebell at thigh level and an end position with the kettlebell racked at the shoulder, inverted, in one hand.
The instructions describe a backswing, a forceful hip-driven reversal, a crushing grip, and raising the bell to the shoulder, which is consistent with the images.

proposed_definition.name: Bottoms-Up Clean From The Hang Position

instructions: Initiate the exercise by standing upright with a kettlebell in one hand.
Swing the kettlebell back forcefully and then reverse the motion forcefully. Crush the kettlebell handle as hard as possible and raise the kettlebell to your shoulder.
